raw_response:
I farm the same 30 mu in wheat-maize rotation, so I will treat it from what worked for me before and adjust a little, not start from zero. I have done this for 50 years in Quzhou, and with well water in hand I do not like to gamble on saving a little fertilizer and then losing yield. On this kind of land, if wheat is short of fertilizer before winter or at jointing, it shows fast, and if maize is hungry at the big bell stage, the ears do not fill well. I will still follow what I did last year and what the better growers around me do: wheat will use improved seed, enough base fertilizer, three irrigations if the weather is normal, and two pesticide sprays. Maize will use hybrid seed, a little heavier nitrogen than wheat, two irrigations, and two pesticide sprays. Since I have 30 mu and only 2 people at home, I will also think about labor, so I will keep the operations simple and use rotary tillage for wheat and no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save time and money. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk cutting production on all 30 mu.
